sentences: A piecewise affine map chooses among finitely many affine update rules according to the region containing the current point.
In one dimension, its orbit is obtained by repeatedly applying this update to a rational starting value.
The question asks whether exact reachability of a rational target is decidable in the general one-dimensional setting, even with only two pieces.
The source contrasts this gap with decidable subclasses and with undecidability already available for unrestricted two-dimensional maps.
Resolving the two-piece case would locate a basic boundary between simple numerical iteration and computations complicated enough to defeat algorithmic reachability analysis.
